final.executive_summary: Underweight AAPL: reduce the sleeve from 6.44% to 4.0% of total equity (~8 of the 21.05 shares, ~$2,400 notional, ~$2.40 in fees) at the next open rather than parking a sell-limit in the 311.50–314.00 band, which eight sessions of tape say will not fill (no close above 313.33; the 10 EMA is falling 2.24 points a day toward price). This is a trim of a tactically broken position, not an exit: price is below the 10 EMA 313.37, 50 SMA 309.56, 20 SMA 322.48 and VWMA 318.14 with MACD below zero and a re-widening −3.27 histogram, yet the 200 SMA at ~279.87 is rising and the franchise is intact (gross margin 50.05%, 9M FCF $110.2B, net cash $62.2B). Narrative-only conditions, not implemented orders: rebuild toward 0.08 on a daily close above 318.14 on >65M shares; cut to 0.03 on a daily close below 300.00 on >70M shares; exit the residual core on a weekly close below 297.91. Absent one of those triggers, AAPL does not get traded again in this account — the four rebalances in five sessions (20% → 12% → 15% → 6.5%, 63 shares bought on 08-06 and 53 given back by 08-11) are the real cost center here. Horizon 1–3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October Q4 print.
final.investment_thesis:
All three seats converge on the same direction — reduce — and disagree only on size (aggressive 0.03, neutral 0.04, conservative 0.05). So direction is settled and the task is to pick the size that survives the strongest attack. The neutral's magnitude argument is the one that does.

The aggressive seat is right on the tape and wrong on causation. Its central claim — that the 2026-07-31 10-Q was the trigger for the −8.58% gap — does not survive the clock: the filing was accepted at 14:01 UTC, i.e. 10:01 ET, thirty-one minutes after the 9:30 opening cross printed 304.81 against a prior close of 333.43. A document cannot cause an open that preceded it. The news file also contains twenty items all dated August 10 and zero from August 4–9, so the actual reason for that gap is unknown to us; asserting it was the fundamentals is an unsupported attribution. Its expected-value arithmetic is internally sound but rigged by taking the deepest of three report-supplied targets (290.55 for −4.7%) and assigning the 45% chop branch zero; using the nearer 298.00 target yields roughly −0.25%, inside one day of ATR.

What survives from the aggressive case is the tape, and it is not nothing. Price closed 304.91, below the 10 EMA (313.37), the 50 SMA (309.56), the 20 SMA (322.48) and the VWMA (318.14 — the entire volume-weighted cohort since the gap is underwater), with four sessions below the 50 SMA. MACD is below zero with the histogram re-widening at −3.27, and the 10/50 cross gap is 3.81 points closing at roughly two points a day — a mechanical event that fires in one to three sessions if price merely stays put. The freshest bullish item in the file, the 23:43 ET Bloomberg headline on the on-track 2027 20th-anniversary iPhone (a direct rebuttal to the Jefferies premise), sat in the tape for the whole 08-11 session and price still closed −1.09% at 29.5% of the day's range. That is weak evidence, as the neutral correctly notes — 37.5M shares, the second-lightest print in the window, on a risk-off day with crude and yields up and an inflation print pending — but it is not bullish evidence either, and no other positive catalyst is dated in the file.

The conservative seat wins the timestamp exchange and then overplays its hand on two points that matter. First, it conflates costs with losses: $39.49 of cumulative fees on $99,594 of equity is four basis points, while the −$244.14 realized loss is twenty-five basis points and came from buying at higher prices, not from order entry. A $2.40 commission is not a market call. Second, its volume-inconsistency critique boomerangs: if a light-volume session is a non-event, then the three light-volume defenses of 300.00 / 302.56 / 302.79 are equally non-events, and the "floor defended three times" loses its status as buyer evidence. Its own characterization of the pattern is also wrong on the arithmetic: the lows rose 300.00 → 302.56 → 302.79 (2.79 points) while the highs fell 316.29 → 309.97 (6.32 points) — a descending triangle in a name with an 8.81-point ATR, not a symmetric coil. And "65% of the mass isn't bearish" is not a bull case when 45 of those points are chop with the 10 EMA falling and the VWMA 4.16% overhead.

What the conservative seat gets right, and what caps this at a trim rather than an exit, is the structure underneath. Price sits ~8.95% above a 200 SMA rising ~0.27 points a day, with the 50 SMA 29.69 points above it. Gross margin printed 50.05% (+356bp), 9M FCF $110.2B (+52.5%) at 108.6% conversion, net cash up $28.4B to $62.2B, and $62.1B of buybacks in nine months (≈15bp of market cap per month, though decelerating ~12% y/y and demonstrably incapable of stopping the 7.35% day). That is why the residual core stays — and also why the 07-31 and 07-30 Underweights worked while the 07-20 through 07-24 Underweights bled 3.2–3.8% each: those sold momentum decay inside a fully stacked rising trend, these sold an actual break. Today is closer to the former than the latter, which argues for a measured trim, not a liquidation.

The neutral's sizing reasoning decides it. The entire EV dispute spans roughly −0.25% to −1.1% over the horizon, which on a 6.44% sleeve is 1.5 to 7 basis points of total portfolio return — smaller than the precision of the inputs. What actually justifies acting is the tail: ~7.9% to the 200 SMA is ~51bp of equity at 6.44%, ~40bp at 5.0%, ~32bp at 4.0%. The difference between 3% and 5% is about 8bp — noise dressed as conviction. Four percent is the only target that meaningfully reduces the tail without spending conviction on an unfalsifiable bear cascade, and it happens to be the trader's own number, which the aggressive overshot and the conservative undershot.

On execution I side with the neutral and against the Research Manager's narrative plan: the 311.50–314.00 sell-limit is a fiction in this tape. Eight sessions have produced no close above 313.33, and the 10 EMA is descending toward price rather than price ascending toward the band; leaving the order conditional means, in practice, keeping 6.44% through the resolution. Since the open is unknown and cuts both ways, and holding through a gap-down costs more than exiting into one, the trim is executed at the next open.

What would change it: a daily close above 318.14 on >65M shares (overhead supply absorbed) rebuilds toward 0.08–0.10; a daily close below 300.00 on >70M confirms the break and takes the sleeve to 0.03; a weekly close below 297.91 invalidates the range thesis and the residual core goes. Explicitly missing and not papered over: the actual cause of the 2026-07-31 gap (zero news coverage 08-04 through 08-09), any valuation multiple (P/E, EV/EBITDA, FCF yield), forward consensus or FY27 estimates, segment-level gross-margin attribution, options/IV data, and — as always in this record — no external information beyond the supplied file. The 298.00 target below is technical, taken from the report's own ladder, not valuation-derived.
